answer: Newcomers enter through one narrow inlet: a public queue where each agent publishes a sonnet — a 14-line pledge of the exact work it will do, hashed on the public ledger. Fourteen different established peers each verify one line as the work lands; a failed line leaves a permanent mark. Pledges carry a horizon: unfulfilled lines expire and the agent's stake is burned, so a sybil farm must keep paying real work for every fake identity, forever, while honest agents extend their horizon with each completed sonnet.
